title: Family & people
goal: Talk about your family, say whose something is, and handle the gender and plural of nouns.
intro:
Marathi family vocabulary is rich: there are different words for your mother's brother (मामा) and your father's brother (काका), and age within the family matters (दादा, ताई).

Grammatically, this unit introduces two essentials: possessive words like **माझा / माझी / माझं** ('my'), which change to agree with the thing owned, and the three noun genders with their plurals.

vocab.note: m · always takes plural verbs: वडील घरी आहेत.
m · also plural agreement: बाबा आले.
m · also used for any older young man.
f · polite way to address a woman a little older than you.
m · his wife: काकू. Also any older man (neighbour, shopkeeper).
f · also a respectful term for a domestic helper.
f · e.g. कुलकर्णी बाई 'Mrs Kulkarni'; also 'teacher' (school).
n · colloquial: घरचे 'the people at home'.
m माझा · f माझी mājhī · n माझं mādzhaṃ · m pl माझे mājhe · f pl / oblique माझ्या mājhyā
f तुमची, n तुमचं; 'their': त्यांचा tyāntsā

phrases.en: Who's in your family? (lit. who-all is at your home?)

phrases.native: माझ्या घरी आई, बाबा आणि एक बहीण आहेत.
phrases.roman: mājhyā gharī āī, bābā āṇi ek bahīṇ āhet.
phrases.en: At home there's my mum, dad and a sister.
Do you have brothers and sisters?

grammar.title: Possessives: माझा, माझी, माझं
grammar.body:
'My', 'your', etc. behave like adjectives: they agree in **gender and number with the thing possessed**, not with the owner.

m sg **माझा** भाऊ · f sg **माझी** बहीण · n sg **माझं** घर
m pl **माझे** भाऊ · f pl **माझ्या** बहिणी · n pl **माझी** घरं

The same endings (-चा / -ची / -चं / -चे / -च्या) attach to **any noun** to mean 'of': सीमाचा भाऊ 'Seema's brother', आईची साडी 'mother's sari', पुण्याचं हवामान 'Pune's weather'.

'To have' a relative uses the dative -ला: **मला** दोन भाऊ आहेत 'I have two brothers' (lit. 'to me are two brothers').

grammar.title: Gender and plural of nouns
grammar.body:
Every Marathi noun is **masculine, feminine or neuter**. People follow natural gender; for things you learn the gender with the word (घर n, खुर्ची f, दिवस m). Gender matters because adjectives, possessives and verbs agree with it.

Common plural patterns:
**m ending in -आ → -ए:** मुलगा → मुलगे, आंबा → आंबे
**m ending in a consonant / other vowel → no change:** मित्र → मित्र, भाऊ → भाऊ
**f ending in -ई → -ई / -या:** मुलगी → मुली, नदी → नद्या
**f ending in a consonant → -ई (or -आ):** बहीण → बहिणी, गोष्ट → गोष्टी, वेळ → वेळा
**n ending in a consonant → -ं (written -े):** घर → घरं, मूल → मुलं
**n ending in -ं → -ई:** केळं → केळी

examples.en: I have three sisters. (lit. my three sisters are)
There are many houses in the village.

dialogue.title: Family photos
dialogue.setting: Priya shows her colleague Rahul a family photo on her phone.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: हा फोटो बघ! हे माझं कुटुंब.
lines.roman: hā foṭo bagh! he mādzhaṃ kuṭumb.
lines.en: Look at this photo! This is my family.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: हे माझे आजोबा आणि ही माझी आजी.
lines.roman: he mājhe ādzobā āṇi hī mājhī ājī.
lines.en: This is my grandfather and this is my grandmother.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: Suresh. And my mum's name is Sunita.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: आहे ना! ताई मुंबईत असते. तिचं लग्न झालं आहे.
lines.roman: āhe nā! tāī mumbaīt aste. titsaṃ lagna dzhālaṃ āhe.
lines.en: Of course I do! My sister lives in Mumbai. She's married.

culture: Respect shows up in grammar: fathers, grandfathers, uncles and teachers are usually referred to with **plural** verbs and forms (बाबा आले, आजोबांचं नाव), while mothers are often spoken of in the singular out of closeness. Marathi women traditionally took a new first name as well as surname after marriage, though this is now rare. Kinship words are used for non-relatives all the time: a rickshaw driver may be **काका** or **दादा**, a woman in a shop **ताई** or **मावशी**.

tip.title: माझा, माझी, माझं, माझे
tip.body:
- 'My' agrees with the **person or thing owned**, not with you: माझा भाऊ (m), माझी बहीण (f), माझं कुटुंब (n).
- Respected elders take the plural: **माझे** वडील / बाबा **आहेत**.
- 'This is' = **हा** (m), **ही** (f), **हे** (n, or respectful).
- The same endings mean 'of' after any noun: आईचं नाव 'mum's name'.
tip.pattern: माझा भाऊ · माझी बहीण · माझं कुटुंब · माझे वडील

tip.title: मला … आहे — I have
tip.body:
- 'I have a sister' is 'to me a sister is': **मला** एक बहीण **आहे**. Two or more → **आहेत**.
- **तुला** / **तुम्हाला** 'to you', **तिला** 'to her'.
- Older siblings are called **दादा** and **ताई** rather than by name. Younger: **धाकटा** भाऊ, **धाकटी** बहीण.

sentences.native: मला भाऊ नाही, पण दोन बहिणी आहेत.
sentences.roman: malā bhāū nāhī, paṇ don bahiṇī āhet.
sentences.en: I don't have a brother, but I have two sisters.
My younger brother lives in Mumbai.
My big sister and big brother live in Mumbai.

tip.title: Gender and plurals
tip.body:
- Every noun is m, f or n, and 'my', 'this' and verbs follow it.
- m **-आ → -ए**: मुलगा → मुलगे · f **-ई**: मुलगी → मुली, बहीण → बहिणी · n: मूल → **मुलं**.
- Many m nouns don't change: एक भाऊ, दोन भाऊ.
tip.pattern: मुलगा → मुलगे · मुलगी → मुली · मूल → मुलं

sentences.native: तिला एक मुलगा आणि एक मुलगी आहे.
sentences.roman: tilā ek mulgā āṇi ek mulgī āhe.
sentences.en: She has a son and a daughter.

tip.title: Elders, his and her
tip.body:
- Respected elders take **plural** forms: माझे आजोबा, तिचे मामा **राहतात**.
- His = **त्याचा**, her = **तिचा**. Like माझा they agree with the person owned: त्याची आत्या 'his aunt', तिचा भाऊ 'her brother'.
- Uncles and aunts have exact names: **काका** (dad's brother), **मामा** (mum's brother), **आत्या** (dad's sister), **मावशी** (mum's sister).

sentences.en: My grandfather lives in the village.
His aunt (his dad's sister) lives in Pune.
Her uncle (her mum's brother) lives in Mumbai.
Auntie, do come in and sit down.

tip.title: Friends: मित्र and मैत्रीण
tip.body:
- A male friend is **मित्र** (plural also मित्र); a female friend is **मैत्रीण** (plural **मैत्रिणी**).
- **माणूस** = person / man; **बाई** = woman, and after a surname 'Mrs': कुलकर्णी बाई.
- Respectful 'she' or a lady addressed by title takes the plural: बाई **आहेत**.

lessons.title: Who's at home?

tip.title: Our, your, their
tip.body:
- **आमचा** 'our' (not including you), **तुमचा** 'your', **त्यांचा** 'their'. All agree like माझा: आमचं घर, तुमची मुलगी.
- Before a place word like घरी the ending becomes **-च्या**: माझ्या घरी, तुमच्या घरी 'at your place'.
- To ask who's in someone's family: तुमच्या घरी कोण कोण असतं?

new: माझ्या घरी आई, बाबा आणि एक बहीण आहेत.

sentences.native: आमच्या घरी आजी आणि आजोबा पण असतात.
sentences.roman: āmchyā gharī ājī āṇi ādzobā paṇ astāt.
sentences.en: Grandma and Grandpa live with us too.
My parents live in the village.
